title: What are the degree measures of the three angles at Q?
description: Three angles at the vertex Q share the arm QP. The protractor is set once with QP on the zero line, and the other three arms are read from that same zero. A check compares the order of the arms with the order of the readings.
teaching_notes: One idea: when angles share an arm, one zero line serves all of them, and a wider angle reads a bigger number. Watch for students who move the zero line to a different arm for each angle.

source: Figure it Out (after Angle Bisector), Q7
video_script.why: The child measures three angles that share an arm by the three checks of the solved example, using the same zero line for all of them.
video_script.substitution: The angles PQR, PQS and PQT of the book's question.
video_script.anchor: the book's drawing of the arms QP, QR, QS and QT from the vertex Q
video_script.payoff_line: Angle pee kew ar measures forty five degrees

final_answer.spoken: forty five degrees, one hundred degrees and one hundred and fifty degrees

maths_rules: check: 45 < 100 < 150, and the arms QR, QS and QT lie further and further from QP
the count starts at 0 on the arm QP that lies on the zero line
video_script.design: The drawing stays on the board. The protractor is set once at Q with QP on the zero line, and the three arms are read one after another; the readings are held back until the answer line.

beats.on_screen: Given: the angles PQR, PQS and PQT, all at the vertex Q and all with the arm QP

beats.on_screen: To find: the degree measures of ∠PQR, ∠PQS and ∠PQT
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the degree measure of each of the three angles.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: put the centre of the protractor on the vertex Q

marks.centre: the protractor slides until its centre point meets Q
marks.why: a tick appears beside the centre point

beats.moves_through: the protractor slides onto the vertex
narration: <bookmark mark='centre'/>Step one, put the centre of the protractor exactly on the vertex kew.
<bookmark mark='why'/>All three angles have their vertex there, so the centre stays there.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: turn the protractor until the arm QP lies along the 0 line

marks.turn: the protractor turns until the arm QP meets the zero line
marks.scale: the scale that starts at that zero is circled
marks.same: the other three arms are shown on the same protractor, without turning it again

beats.moves_through: the protractor turns about the vertex
narration: <bookmark mark='turn'/>Step two, turn the protractor until the arm kew pee lies along the zero line.
<bookmark mark='scale'/>We read the scale that starts at that zero.
<bookmark mark='same'/>All three angles share this arm, so one zero line serves all three.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: read the number where each of the arms QR, QS and QT crosses the scale

marks.again: the arms QS and QT are followed out to the scale in the same way

narration: <bookmark mark='read'/>Step three, follow the arm kew ar out to the scale and read the number.
<bookmark mark='again'/>Then read the arms kew ess and kew tee the same way.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check the order; an arm that lies further from QP must read a bigger number

marks.order: the arms are lined up from the nearest to the farthest from QP
marks.check: a tick appears when the readings grow in the same order

narration: <bookmark mark='order'/>Step four, check the order of the arms.
<bookmark mark='check'/>An arm that lies further from kew pee must read a bigger number.

marks.ans: the reading of PQR is boxed
marks.second: the reading of PQS is boxed
marks.third: the reading of PQT is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Angle pee kew ar measures forty five degrees.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Angle pee kew ess measures one hundred degrees.
